# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 5
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 5

---

*[THE TALKING COLT.]*

1. Thomas left Gundaphorus and his brother and set out for the next city.

2. He was walking along the road when a wild ass's colt came up to him and spoke. "Twin of Christ," it said. "Fellow apostle — why are you walking? You're exhausting yourself for nothing. Get on my back."

3. Thomas stopped and stared at the animal. "Who taught you to talk?" he said.

4. "I come from the line of the ass that carried your Lord into Jerusalem," the colt said. "I was kept for just this moment — so that you could ride me, just as he rode my ancestor. It is right that those who carry the word should ride on asses."

5. Thomas smiled. "Well said," he told the colt.

6. He climbed on and they rode. They went a long distance.

7. The people on the road stared. A wild ass — carrying a man? They couldn't stop watching.

8. They reached an inn and the colt carried Thomas inside.

9. Thomas got down.

10. The colt said: "Apostle of Christ the Most High — your sign has been completed. You have what you needed.

11. Now — I ask this of you — let me go home. I cannot eat your food or drink your water."

12. "The one who gave you your voice," Thomas said, "will lead you home."

13. The colt bowed its head before Thomas and walked away.

14. Thomas watched it go. Then he lifted his voice and thanked God for the wonders that kept appearing in front of him.

---
*PNEUMA note: The talking colt's lineage from the Palm Sunday ass is one of the most charming episodes in the apocryphal acts. It draws a direct line from the Lord's triumphal entry to Thomas's mission — the apostle as the extension of Christ into the world. "Twin of Christ" (*taw'ma d'Mshiha*) is the text's own pun on Thomas's name. The colt's polite request to go home ("I cannot eat your food") is a moment of earthy, tender comedy.*
